entry.title: EA Sports FC 26 release date and crossplay info, leaked

The release date for EA Sports FC 26, or EA FC 26 in short, is doing the rounds on social media.
While EA Sports has revealed nothing official yet, a new leak has emerged on X from AhcanFUT, who's a reliable name in the community. EA Sports FC 26 release date (leaked)
If the rumors are to be believed, EA FC 26 will be released on August 23 for Ultimate Edition users. If EA Sports follows the same pattern that they did for FC 25, the full launch will take place on August 30. The Ultimate Edition, as usual, is expected to have several benefits, including early access.

EA Sports could end up giving us the first trailer for the upcoming game, but it's better to wait for official information before reaching a conclusion.
EA Sports FC 26 crossplay changes
EA FC 26 is expected to be released on both generations of consoles, along with PC. EA Sports will likely offer special editions for the Nintendo Switch and the Nintendo Switch 2. While crossplay between the same generational devices will be there, console and PC users will no longer be able to play together.
This will be a major change from how crossplay works in EA FC 25. In the current game, those on the current generation consoles of Xbox and PlayStation can match with and against PC users. EA Sports is finally set to make the much requested change after all.
It's worth noting that all the information presented in the article are in the form of leaks. Readers are advised to take the news with a grain of salt, and some of the actual meaning of the original tweet could have been lost in translation.

entry.title: What to do with Swim Trunks in Blue Prince?
entry.summary:
The Swim Trunks is one of the many items you can come across in Blue Prince, but the game doesn't tell you anything about what to do with them.
The chance of this item spawning is based on luck, so if you have found it, consider yourself lucky. They are used later in a spoiler tied with the Pool room. This guide will provide you with all the important info regarding the trunks if you manage to find them on your save.
What do the Swim Trunks in Blue Prince?
The Swim Trunks on their own don't have any use. You can neither use them nor combine them to produce something else. That doesn't automatically mean that they're completely useless. In fact, finding these trunks will automatically spawn something in the Pool room.
The Pool usually has coins available at the bottom. They will be replaced by a couple of floating Trunks (the container, not the Swim Trunks). You can open these trunks through a couple of different methods.
How to open Locked Trunks in Blue Prince?
The first way is to use keys to open them. Ordinary keys will work just fine, but it's better to save them to open doors. Opening doors in Blue Prince is far more important, as it will get you closer to your final goal.
Image via Dogubomb
A better method is to use the sledgehammers. You can find this item in certain rooms, but it ultimately depends on luck. In case you can't find one in your room, you can just buy them from the Commissary. While this method requires Gold Coins, it's far more effective. Moreover, once you buy the Sledgehammer, you can use it as many times as you like.
Trunks can include valuable items in them, including Gold Coins and Dice. It's all down to luck on what you might get. If you'd like to see more, here are all the items and their locations in Blue Prince.

What are badges, you ask? Badges are something add-on (NewGRF) authors can put on their content to help you find e.g. the vehicle or station you want to use. For example, various vehicle add-ons use a mix of different icons, overlay images or texts to indicate the power source or the suggested usage of a vehicle. With badges, this information can be represented in a clear way including built-in filtering, that is cohesive between different add-ons. As this beta is the first release featuring badge support, there aren’t many updated add-ons yet, but we’re excited to see what authors do with the new feature. entry.title: Orbifold is an anti-gravity shooter set inside a giant sphere that looks like a really wild Halo level
entry.summary: Back in 2020, Half-Life: Alyx developer Robin Walker told Katharine (RPS in peace) that one of the hardest things in first-person shooter development is persuading people to look up. "One of the problems you always run into in an FPS is that players are really good at looking horizontally with their mouse, but they don't look up and down nearly as much," said Walker. "You've really got to work to make a player look up in FPS games." You will definitely need to look up in Orbifold, a forthcoming shooter project from Hi-Rez programmer Chris Cullen. In this Unreal Engine 5 creation, firefights take place inside a giant, verdant ball akin to a miniature Dyson Sphere, but with no captive star. Players are gravitationally rooted to the exterior of the ball, meaning you can run all the way around the inside. There are also Halo-style launchers that punt you directly through the middle. entry.title: Prey director is optimistic genAI could help immersive sims by acting like a "Dungeons & Dragons GM"
entry.summary: In a recent episode of the Quad Damage podcast, Arkane founder Raphaël Colantonio spoke about his ideas for a new Dishonored game. He, Harvey Smith, and Dinga Bakaba all had their own ideas for a sequel, he said, although the odds of any of them being developed are low as all three devs now work on different projects. Elsewhere on the podcast, the subject turned to Colantonio's thoughts on AI and the future of immersive sims. In short, he sounds optimistic. "If AI could really remember everything, and take meaningful human decisions like a Dungeons and Dragons Gamemaster, then that would actually be very valuable. Things we could not do. There would not be a team that is big enough to do this kind of thing." "One of the things about immersive sims is that we are always trying, either to plan for everything that we think the player might do - and that's authoring, that's painful," Colantonio said. "Or, we're doing a lot of failsafes with systems that somehow fall back on their feet if the player does something we did not plan. There's always some stuff the players do that we haven't planned, so that's why you have the net under. But that net's a little janky. Sometimes it works, sometimes not." Read more

entry.title: FromSoftware multiplayer is best when it's a secret
entry.summary:
Let me start this with the memory that always surfaces when I write about Dark Souls multiplayer - the anecdote I’ve told in several articles, hoping that somebody (you?) will explain. It’s 2011 and I’m making my way through Lordran for the first time. I’m in the woods with my longsword and Grass Crest Shield. There is a glimmer through the trees and another player appears, wearing exotic equipment. I raise my guard, anticipating a swift defeat, but the other player only stands and waves. They beckon me deeper into the wood. It’s rarely smart to follow a stranger into the woods. I do so anyway, keeping my distance, shield held out like a passport, and am led to a clearing in which another player kneels. The second player does not react to my arrival. The first player gesticulates urgently.
